A beneficial approach for gathering user insights while safeguarding user anonymity exists in federated learning. Nonetheless, novel classes emerging from unseen data patterns during the training process pose a challenge for this method. These new classes necessitate discovery and incorporation into the existing classification model. We investigate two distinct methods for incorporating these new classes: a data-driven method utilizing autoencoders to isolate novel data patterns, and a model-based method using clustering techniques to group training data based on model outputs. Both methods were applied and evaluated in a federated context, employing audio datasets "ESC:50" and "UrbanSound8K" to classify various environmental sounds.

A comprehensive theoretical model is offered in this paper for analyzing high-dimensional entangled systems, specifically the Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger state. Initially, we apply our approach to measure a complete three-photon GHZ state across three dimensions and then extend it to multi-photon systems within higher dimensional settings. In our model, both hyperentanglement of photons and the quantum Fourier transform are employed. The proposed solution will serve as a useful resource for developing high-dimensional quantum computation and communication.

This research paper delves into the problem of uplink cascaded channel estimation in multi-user multiple-input-single-output systems aided by intelligent-reflecting-surfaces operating within the sub-6 GHz frequency range where channel propagation isn't sparse. A high-performance, low-overhead estimation protocol has been developed to minimize reflection power loss without requiring on-off amplitude control. The proposed solution exploits a common structure within the system, significantly reducing pilot transmission overhead by decomposing the complex cascaded channel into separate user-specific and shared variables. The challenge of highly coupled estimation variables is overcome through the use of optimization-based estimation methods utilizing channel covariance. An alternating optimization algorithm has been developed to efficiently solve the resulting non-convex problem, with an efficient initialization step enabled by a proposed sample collection protocol. A simplified, efficient scheme has also been developed for the specific scenario of single-antenna users and MISO structure. Comprehensive simulation results validate the proposed protocol's superiority over existing benchmark solutions in terms of pilot overhead and estimation distortion.

This study analyzes data from an online monitoring system of U.S. local news to explore connections between COVID coverage, regional case and death rates, and characteristics of news outlets and their audiences. Using a distinct dataset of over 750,000 articles from over 300 outlets between April 2020 and February 2021, our results show that local news outlets initially covered COVID at a rate influenced by national death rates but ultimately became less correlated as other factors prevailed. Moreover, our research reveals that local news COVID coverage varied based on the area's politics, news outlet popularity, and audience size, and also indicates that some outlets emphasized mortality rates while others focused on other aspects, such as the economy. Ultimately, our findings indicate that local news COVID coverage was not solely determined by regional COVID metrics but rather was influenced by a complex interplay of factors.

The fundamental ability to count is a prime example of humans' innate capacity for abstract thinking. In this ability, there's typically a notable turning point where children rapidly grasp and master counting techniques. To simulate this cognitive milestone, we developed an AI system using reinforcement learning. By testing this system with tasks similar to those used in psychological research, we discovered that it exhibited a period of rapid learning analogous to children's "counting explosion." Additionally, our model like human children, developed subtle yet obvious biases, such as a preference for counting methods over others. In line with theoretical predictions, our results show that these biases arise naturally from the interplay between the reinforcement learning algorithm and the representation of numbers in the model.

Bloom filters provide quick approximations of set membership while consuming minimal memory. These filters help engineers prevent time-consuming actions, such as accessing a disk or the network. A potential substitute for Bloom filters is the cuckoo filter, which often needs less storage and processes information faster. A different solution, the Bloomier filter, has been proposed as an expansion of the Bloom filter. A modification to this concept has also been explored, particularly by Dietzfelbinger and Pagh. A different approach was taken by O'Neil and Guentner, leading to the creation of Bloomier filters through van Dijk, O'Neil, and Ashdown. A different extension to the Bloom filter is the HyperLogLog sketch, developed by Flajolet and others, with further work by Brunel, Jeanmarie, and other scientists. Several key connections between convex geometry and holomorphic line bundles on smooth projective varieties or K\"ahler manifolds are explored. Our investigation focuses on the relationship between positive products and mixed volumes, leading to the establishment of new equivalence relationships. Furthermore, building on a previous finding by the second author, we extend it by demonstrating that the equivalence between a combination of nef and ample classes and the strict convexity of a polytope can be reciprocated when the real coefficients are substituted with rational coefficients.

A new approach aims to derive market trend insights from dynamic price equations, specifically those that describe how future market values are influenced by past trading activity. To achieve this, a novel filter is designed to extract relevant time segments from the trading history, producing a share price dynamic that incorporates both past and future market behaviors. By comparing initial share values with their predicted values based on the trading sequence, a dynamic price ratio is generated for each trading period. This ratio serves as a key indicator of the underlying market trend.

This work presents FLVoogd, a refined federated learning technique that allows servers and clients to cooperatively prevent Byzantine attacks while maintaining user anonymity. Specifically, servers utilize DBSCAN with S2PC to cluster the legitimate data majority without acquiring private user data. Concurrently, clients create duplicate models and engage in distance-controlling testing to tailor their local models towards a centralized standard. Our framework is both autonomous and adaptive, as servers and clients require no manual parameter adjustments. Furthermore, it relies on SMPC operations such as multiplication, addition, and comparison, which omits expensive operations like division and square root. Evaluation on standard image classification datasets demonstrates that FLVoogd effectively blocks malicious submissions and precludes data exposure from the server.

We successfully submitted the winning entry to the NeurIPS 2021 - AWS Deepracer challenge, which required developing a self-driving vehicle model that interacts with its environment through action-reward interactions. The objective was to create an autonomous vehicle model that navigates a simulated track, adapts to real-world settings, and completes a lap at maximum speed while staying on course. The competition was part of The AI Driving Olympics (AI-DO), a series that fosters embodied intelligence advancements in autonomous driving, by benchmarking the progress in applied autonomy. The Deepracer challenge proved to be complex, especially when translating skills from simulated to real-world settings, so we implemented a two-pronged approach to bridge the domain gap in visual observations and control dynamics. We leveraged image gradient information to establish a connection between simulated and real-world settings, and combined it with a multi-fork actor-learning approach to ensure stable skill adaptation. The key to our success was directly utilizing image gradient signals, thus avoiding tedious data augmentation and ground-truth acquisition, while also reducing training and inference times. We observed a notable increase in vehicle speed and consistency thanks to our gradient-based signal feature, and ultimately achieved an overall reward of 347.95, with our model completing the lap in approximately 18.83 seconds, with a reward of 347.95 in the real-world setting.

Significant progress in deep learning technology has enabled the creation of more convincingly authentic deepfakes, which have sparked interest across multiple sectors due to their vast applications, despite raising serious societal and security risks. This chapter examines the advancements and difficulties in the production and identification of deepfakes, and also explores the potential solutions to improve the resilience of deepfake detection for a broad range of media, such as real-world images and videos. Furthermore, it proposes future research directions for tackling deepfake-related issues.

The identification of sub-Neptune exoplanets receiving irradiance levels similar to Earth's revitalized the prospect of discovering potentially habitable worlds over the coming decade, with some temperate planets potentially harboring liquid water oceans, provided they do not possess massive H2/He envelopes that would cause them to be excessively hot. Characterizing the masses of these envelopes in planets with large radii, however, poses a challenge. We demonstrate that observable differences in atmospheric transit signatures could distinguish between two distinct scenarios regarding the mass of a temperate sub-Neptune's envelope: one with a small mass where carbon and nitrogen are provided primarily by the delivery of solid bodies, versus one with a higher mass where these elements are primarily produced through thermal breakdown of carbon-rich molecules and organic solids. The presence of a small vs. large envelope mass would manifest respectively as a milder or more intense signature in the planet's atmospheric transmission spectrum, due to the resulting differences in atmospheric pressure and temperature. The distinction between these scenarios could be discerned through recent breakthroughs in spectroscopic techniques that can detect the differences in atmospheric transmission spectra at wavelengths of a few thousand, as opposed to tens of thousands, Earth mass. Conversely, the mass of a temperate sub-Neptune's envelope could also be inferred through the observation of baric temperature effects, where an increased mass would manifest as a notable increase in temperature with decreasing pressure towards the upper atmosphere. Inspired by the classic discrete-time model of nervous activity proposed by McCulloch and Pitts in 1943, a new continuous-time model, known as the McCulloch-Pitts network (MPN), has been developed for sequence learning in spiking neural networks. This model employs a localized learning rule, in which synaptic weights update solely based on the accessible information at each synapse. The model leverages the consistency of neural responses over time by adjusting the weight change coefficient, thereby facilitating efficient sequence memorization. Furthermore, our study reveals that MPN shares similarities with both the fundamental leaky-integrator neural network and the fundamental temporal difference learning algorithm. The model's effectiveness has been demonstrated through both theoretical and empirical evidence, showing that MPN outperforms the basic backpropagation algorithm in tasks such as memorizing random sequences and recognizing spoken numbers in speech, while also producing biologically plausible results.

This paper reports on the findings from the 2022 Out-Of-Vocabulary (OOV) challenge.
The competition highlighted an underinvestigated area in Optical Character Recognition (OCR) technology: accurately reading previously unseen text in real-world images during model training.
The dataset compiled for the competition comprises a diverse collection of 326,385 images, encompassing 4,864,405 text instances.
To address the challenge, a distinct validation and test set was created, comprising scene text that was not present in the training data.
The competition featured two recognition tasks: a holistic approach to reading full text and a focused task involving cropped text segments.
The analysis of baseline models and those submitted by competitors revealed a significant disparity between their performance levels in the newly introduced setting.
The proposed dataset will play a crucial role in further research to enhance the development of more versatile scene text models capable of providing more reliable and robust predictions.

A specific type of chaos expansions can effectively analyze differential equations with uncertain factors by approximating random equilibrium states associated with such equations. This study integrates principles from validated calculations to provide precise error assessments alongside findings about chaos expansions representing random equilibrium states. This approach also develops a new framework for validated tracking, which entails accurately calculating separate solution branches in parameter-dependent systems and generalizes seamlessly to multi-parameter tracking. To demonstrate the proposed methodology, this research achieves the precise calculation of random equilibrium cycles in the Lorenz system, as well as solution branches and 2-dimensional planes of steady states in the Swift-Hohenberg equation.

The increased use of sensors in industrial settings has led to the widespread collection of high-dimensional data, despite this comes with its own set of difficulties. Notably, gathering a comprehensive set of readings is challenging due to the inherent limitations of sensors and available resources. Moreover, industrial systems may exhibit multiple failure patterns, and identifying the primary cause is essential. This work aims to develop an adaptive monitoring system capable of handling high-dimensional data in resource-scarce environments. Our proposed solution incorporates the Shiryaev-Roberts method at the core of a multi-arm approach, where each arm corresponds to a particular failure mode, and a Shorley-like strategy is used to determine when to investigate a new arm. A theoretical framework for establishing the probability of correct isolation is presented, along with a condition to ensure the dominance of the first failure pattern. This framework enables the parameter estimation required to implement the proposed multi-arm approach. Through numerical experiments and a case study, our method's effectiveness will be demonstrated.

We have created a detailed analysis of the origins and development of two disrupted galaxies that merged with the Milky Way's outer layers: the Gaia-Sausage Enceladus (GSE) and Wukong/LMS-1 systems. Our sophisticated computational model, designed to simulate galaxy growth patterns, is based on exponential infall scenarios with varying rates and timing of star formation controlled by parameters. By leveraging Bayesian techniques and observational data including stellar ages, chemical compositions, and metallicities, we identify the most suitable models and identify key parameters for each system. For the GSE system, our results reveal a single infall event with a uniform rate of star formation occurring over 2 billion years and with metallicity progression, while also capturing the observed trends of chemical enrichment. Conversely, the Wukong/LMS-1 system was subject to multiple infall events with distinct rates and varying intervals of star formation activity, along with an internal spread of metallicity dispersion. Our models successfully reproduce observed patterns of chemical element abundance by identifying specific star formation patterns and incorporating factors such as distance from the plane of the galaxy and degree of nitrogen enrichment. For the GSE system, a close relationship between aluminum and silicon abundances is accurately modeled, while for Wukong/LMS-1, our models reveal a double sequence split by 1 Gyr and characterized by different oxygen and silicon abundances in the outer galaxy layer. These findings support the idea that the GSE system experienced a single, uniform star

Given a profinite group G, an S[[G]]-module is a G-spectrum that fulfills certain criteria, leading to the definition of the homotopy orbit spectrum X_{hG} associated with an S[[G]]-module X. When X's constituents meet specific finiteness criteria, a homotopy orbit spectral sequence arises with an E2-term being the continuous homology of G, taking coefficients from the graded profinite \widehat{\mathbb{Z}}[[G]]-module \pi_*(X). This is demonstrated with an equivalence for certain conditions on G and Z: specifically, (Z[[G]])_{hG} is shown to be equivalent to Z in those scenarios, with supplementary methods for further investigation provided.

A major challenge in creating AI models that can extract data from documents is the cost of labeling them. To overcome this issue, we've developed a system that efficiently uses human input: instead of having humans provide full document annotations, we ask for limited, short-range labels. These short-range labels are then used to train the AI model, which can subsequently perform long-range tasks on its own. We've tested this approach, which we call 'decoupled labeling', across multiple publicly available datasets and found that it significantly reduces labeling costs, with only minimal impact on performance. Specifically, compared to traditional end-to-end labeling methods, our approach reduces labeling costs by a factor of 3.5 to 7.5, depending on the dataset.

The EuS/InAs interface has gained attention due to its potential to introduce magnetic properties in a semiconductor material crucial for the development of quantum devices. Using a computational model that incorporates machine-learned data and density functional theory, we have studied how varying the bonding configuration at the interface impacts the electronic properties. Across the examined configurations, we observed that the energy levels at the interface in InAs are positioned higher than those in EuS. Furthermore, we discovered new states that arise from the interaction between the two materials, and are localized at the interface due to charge transfer. The arrangement of atoms at the interface influences both the energy position and distribution of these states. Additionally, we evaluated the stability of each configuration by calculating the work of adhesion and dissipation strength at the interface. Our results indicate that the stability of the interface depends on the bonding configuration, which in turn influences the electronic properties and potential magnetic coupling between EuS and InAs.

A comprehensive classification system for subsets of Baire space, categorized by Borel Wadge classes, has been introduced with enhanced effectiveness. Based on Montalbán's true stage machinery, we leverage this innovation to offer an alternative demonstration of Louveau and Saint-Raymond's separation theorem. This leads to a demonstration of Borel Wadge determinacy within the $\text{ATR}_0+\Pi^1_1$-I system of second-order arithmetic.

Deep, wide, and complex Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are emerging due to rising demands for accurate results and thorough analyses. However, they necessitate a considerable amount of computational power and time for processing. Previous studies on pruning have focused on enhancing inference efficiency, but there's been limited research on effectively decreasing training costs. Our proposed framework, ClickTrain, efficiently and accurately enables both end-to-end training and model pruning for CNNs, distinguishing itself from previous work with fine-grained architecture preservation through pattern-based pruning, precise weight estimation, and compiler-optimized calculations. As a result, ClickTrain can deploy high-accuracy and fast-pruned models directly without additional overhead compared to traditional methods, while also minimizing the pruning-after-training approach by up to 2.3 times with similar results and up to 2.3 times with the pruning-during-training approach with both higher results and efficient pruning results, all under equivalent time constraints.

This research examines the properties of specific modal logics derived from noncommutative lattices by incorporating $\Box$ and $\Diamond$. A new semantics model is introduced, specifically tailored for substructural modal logics. By applying duality principles, we demonstrate that every modal logic derived from the full Lambek calculus has a Kripke model, if it adheres to a specific structural rule. Furthermore, we establish a dual relationship between certain mathematical structures, specifically modal algebras and topological spaces with frames.

The collaborations of the Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory and Virgo have observed the full spectrum of merging compact binaries, which comprise binary black hole, binary neutron star, and neutron star-black hole events. Combining these detections with electromagnetic radiation holds significant potential to improve our comprehension of neutron star events, particularly their dense matter state. However, electromagnetic analysis of gravitational waves necessitates the rapid identification of signals from gravitational waves in real-time. Traditional approaches struggle to achieve this level of speed and efficiency. We introduce novel results based on a deep learning method called BOTO, which utilizes a binary-based, neural-based algorithm for detecting signals among background noise. We have expanded BOTO to accommodate the most recent LIGO-Virgo benchmark signals, which include the most intricate neutron star-black hole mergers. Following a thorough training, BOTO has consistently outperformed the standard reference detector, demonstrating exceptional accuracy and efficiency. On the detection of the most intense signals, BOTO excels, particularly when there is a distinct space-based detector involved. Therefore, deep learning-based methods like BOTO have the potential to significantly enhance the real-time analysis of gravitational waves.

A new discovery has been made regarding a gas giant exoplanet, which orbits around a star called TOI-5542 approximately every 75 days. Initially detected by the TESS satellite, the exoplanet, which has a radius similar to that of Jupiter, has been further confirmed using data from ground-based spectrographic equipment. Analysis of this data has shown that the exoplanet, which has an estimated mass roughly equivalent to that of Jupiter, likely formed through migration or by remaining in its original location rather than being formed by a specific high-energy migration mechanism. Further study found that the host star, which is approximately 10 billion years old, has a metal composition that deviates from a commonly recognized trend of metal-rich giant planets being formed around metal-rich host stars. Interestingly, this study found that both heavy and lightweight gas giants orbiting either warm or hot stars have higher-than-average metal compositions. TOI-5542b is a notable addition to studies of planetary composition due to its relatively cool temperature, which prevents it from expanding in size as a result of exposure to its star's heat.

Sequential decision-making in operations management problems, such as those governed by constraints, can be addressed using the constrained Markov decision process (CMDP). Two main obstacles arise when attempting to solve CMDPs for the development of optimal operational strategies: they are often characterized by an extremely vast number of states and actions, as well as a difficult-to-compute transition matrix. To resolve these challenges, we develop an algorithm that combines policy iteration with subgradient ascent. We show that this approach allows the CMDP to converge to a solution at a rate proportional to $O(\log(T)/\sqrt{T})$, where T represents the number of iterations, provided that a specific condition is met. This method also offers an efficient way to reduce the dimensionality of the CMDP by exploiting its structural properties when applicable. We successfully apply our algorithm to critical problems with such a structure: multi-product inventory control and multi-class queue management, achieving results superior to state-of-art methods.

This research outlines a method for recognizing handwritten mathematical symbols when not using an actual input device, offline. The approach involves segmenting symbols accurately into over 300 categories. Since many complex mathematical symbols require both horizontal and vertical projection to be split, but certain symbols, like most curves, cannot be processed this way, a proposed size and horizontal/vertical projection sizing method is introduced to help resolve the issue. The feasibility of the proposed method was tested with 300 symbols, dividing them into 11 groups to simplify recognition. Results showed that offline recognition was possible with high precision, reaching up to 75%. The study demonstrated effective symbol segmentation using vertical and horizontal projection methods and introduced a new approach to categorizing symbols based on their shape and structure to improve recognition accuracy.

A geometric interpretation is provided for superconformal quantum mechanics based on a hyper-Kahler cone that has a symplectic resolution with equivariant symplectic properties. In this framework, BPS states can be represented as specific cohomology classes in twisted Dolbeault cohomology on the resolved space. The growth rates of BPS state degeneracies, specifically their indices, are connected to Euler characteristic computations in equivariant sheaf cohomology. A notable instance is when considering the Hilbert scheme of points on a 2D plane; this yields an accurate calculation of exponential BPS state degeneracy growth rates as the number of points goes to infinity. The growth characteristics serve as a theoretical prototype for the duality concept we introduced between a 7D black hole and superconformal quantum mechanics.

We examine the relationship between network architecture and disease propagation in the contact process using numerical methods. Initially, our research reveals that the disparity in epidemic behavior between homogeneous and heterogeneous networks is surprisingly small, yet the latter's complex structure can lead to a lower overall infection rate. This outcome contrasts with our expectation, as the enhanced variability in heterogeneous networks should theoretically increase the contact process's exponential decay rate. To clarify this discrepancy, we conduct an in-depth analysis of the probability currents and find that the phenomenon is attributed to a higher concentration of system components in the low-energy ground state. Specifically, the distribution of energy states in heterogeneous networks allows a significantly higher percentage of system components to occupy the low-energy vortex state, resulting in reduced kinetic activity and lower infection rates. Moreover, our research shows that the variability in network architecture can affect the contact process's critical exponent through the system's local spatial homogeneity, with the highest critical exponent observed in star networks and the lowest in the complete graph. Additionally, our research explores the impact of multiple disease types and the interplay between different epidemic propagation mechanisms.

Actor-critic reinforcement learning is commonly employed in robotics due to its versatility, but it can be difficult to optimize effectively. Incorporating a Hamiltonian Monte Carlo framework for exploring action spaces may help overcome this challenge, though the current approach for integrating HMC within the actor-critic framework has been shown to provide only minor improvements. A potential limitation of previous HMC implementations has been the assumption that P_Pi (the derivative of the policy function) is available analytically, which is not typically the case. As a result, previous methods have involved approximating P_Pi through numerical differentiation, a less preferred approach. A new and more accurate variant of the HMC-actor-critic framework has been developed to circumvent this issue, replacing numerical differentiation with an optimization-based technique for estimating P_Pi. The novel method has been named Adaptive Actor-Explorer (AAE) and has been put through its paces with a range of challenging robotic tasks, the success of which suggests that AAE is a viable alternative to traditional actor-critic frameworks, with the potential to outperform in tasks that are a mix of easy and difficult actions.

It's widely recognized that any prime number $p$ greater than or equal to $5$ can be represented as either $6k-1$ or $6k+1$. We will refer to the number $k$ that produces a given prime $p$ as the $\textbf{generator}$ of that prime. Pairs of twin primes have the unique characteristic of sharing a $\textbf{common generator}$. As a result, searching for these twin primes at the level of their respective generators makes practical sense. This paper introduces a novel strategy for verifying the $\textbf{Twin Prime Conjecture}$ by utilizing a sieving approach to extract all twin primes at their generator level and then demonstrating that the sequence of their associated generator values converges towards a fixed point. In a related study, we develop a framework for establishing the existence of the $\textbf{Prime Number Theorem}$ using an iterative method rooted in the $\textbf{Erdős-Száll Self-Contained Proof}$ and show that this approach can be applied to yield an $\textbf{Erdős-Kac Distribution}$ of number $n$ for which there are exactly one, two, three, or four prime numbers less than or equal to it. Autonomous navigation in diverse and ever-changing indoor spaces poses a significant challenge for mobile robots. In poor weather conditions or when surfaces are obstructed, conventional sensing technologies may struggle to operate effectively and provide reliable data for secure route planning. This research aims to tackle the problem of indoor navigation in unstructured environments by designing a mobile robot system that efficiently processes multiple sensory inputs and makes navigation decisions in real-time. To achieve this, we have developed an innovative layered controller for a mobile robot equipped with sonar sensors, capable of operating in dynamic environments and providing a seamless indoor navigation experience. A high-level controller leverages a modified D* algorithm to optimize path planning, while a low-level Layered Motion Controller handles the details of movement. To test the system's robustness and navigational accuracy, a series of simulations and real-world trials were conducted using a sonar-equipped robot. The results of these experiments demonstrate the success of our approach in facilitating secure and efficient navigation within complex and dynamic indoor environments.

Nereid, a satellite of Neptune that holds the distinction of being the largest outer satellite that can be spectroscopically analyzed, exhibits an irregular orbit. Our analysis focuses on Nereid's spectral characterization utilizing its reflectance spectrum between 0.8-2.4 $\mu m$, particularly in the unexplored 0.8-1.4 $\mu m$ range, as we attempt to identify the spectral absorption features that correspond to its icy composition. Our findings indicate the presence of crystalline water ice, coinciding with existing observations. Nonetheless, using simple Tholen-McKinnon CMAN matrix compositions, we are unable to obtain a match between observed and calculated spectra, implying the presence of additional components. Given the analysis of Nereid's entire reflectance spectrum, our model includes a mixture of crystalline water ice, carbonates, and NaCl, in addition to organic compounds, providing a comprehensive spectral fit. Our models for Nereid's surface composition are sensitive to several parameters, specifically the size and distribution of fine-grained water ice particles, free CI radicals, and carbonates, as well as the presence of deliquated brine layers on top of cohesive water ice. Carbonates are found to significantly influence the shape of Nereid's reflectance spectrum within the 0.8-1.4 $\mu m$ range, while NAI and KI 1$\mu m$ absorption bands are ruled out by our analysis

Let $\mathcal{R}_n(q)$ be the ring of lower triangular matrices of order $n \geq 2$, consisting of elements from the finite field $F(q)$ of order $q \geq 2$. Additionally, let $V_{2n}(q)$ be the free left module of its counterpart ${^2T_n(q)}$. Studies have proven that over the projective line based on $T_n(q)$, we find $(q+1)^{(n-1)}q^{\frac{3(n-1)(n-2)}{2}}$ affine planes of order $q$, where points and lines within such a plane satisfy specific submodule properties. These affine planes are ultimately shown to be extendable to a projective plane of order $q$, where free cyclic submodules corresponding to non-unimodular pairs form the projective line's geometry. This approach offers the possibility of generalizing this concept to arbitrary $n$ in a direct manner.

In a 1986 paper in J. Symbolic Logic, Pawlikowski demonstrated that under specific conditions regarding Cohen and random reals, certain model properties can be inferred within extensions of those models. This is proven through a novel application of Tukey-order with models, expanding upon an existing concept introduced by Vojtáš in 1991.

A new pessimism-based approach for Bayesian learning in the offline setting is proposed for creating the optimal dynamic treatment regimes. Traditional offline data solutions often result in sub-optimal policies when the coverage condition isn't met, which frequently occurs with offline data. The pessimism principle resolves this problem by limiting actions that aren't supported by the data, but most pessimism-based methods have limitations such as only working in high-dimensional settings, requiring specific data properties, or imposing structural assumptions on the data. The newly suggested approach, which involves a pessimism-based Bayesian least squares polynomial estimator, has several benefits, including its capacity to handle a large number of potential actions, its ability to perform well in both high and low dimensions, and its ability to function without specific data properties. The proposed approach can efficiently learn the optimal treatment regime in non-convex action spaces with both theoretical and practical justification. The theoretical justification is based on the design of the pessimism-based Bayesian least squares polynomial estimator, which enables efficient learning of the optimal treatment regime with both finite and infinite number of potential actions. The practical justification is based on its application in two case studies with real data.

Dualities between subcategories of finitely generated modules over Artin algebras can be defined by the relationship to Wakamatsu tilting bimodules, with specific cases yielding known dualities. When restricting these relationships to subcategories of finitely generated modules with particular dimensions, previously established correspondences and dualities on tilting modules are reaffirmed. The implications of this relationship include demonstrating equivalences of derived categories of finitely generated Gorenstein-projective modules, as well as the invariance of certain algebraic invariants under tilting transformations.

A study has shown that a specific subset of $E_8$ vectors in 8-dimensional space plays a crucial role in managing the level of quantum entanglement present. Research revealed that the level of entanglement can be controlled through displacement in 4-dimensional space and then projected back onto the original 8-dimensional space. The results indicated that this entanglement can reach extreme levels, corresponding to a maximum of 128 times the entanglement found in the original $E_8$ space. The study further demonstrated that these findings apply universally to any 8-dimensional space based on the $E_8$ root system, offering a valuable framework for future research.

In a flat band superconductor, bosonic modes can freely propagate whereas unpaired electrons are fixed in place. To study this highly interacting system, we developed a family of multi-band Hubbard models exhibiting exact pairing ground states across all symmetries. Through analytical computations, we discovered that many-body excitations are governed by an effective single-particle Hamiltonian based on the non-interacting wave functions of the system. Furthermore, we found a zero-energy excitation characteristic to these bound states with dispersion determined by the minimal quantum metric. Additionally, we observed both bound and free collective modes depending on the topology of the superconductor.

The Gaussian distribution is uniquely determined by the distribution of a linear combination and a power function of independent identically distributed random variables. We identify the a-adic solenoids for which this relationship holds, effectively proving a theorem analogous to the generalized Polya theorem. This proof relies on solving a functional equation for a specific class of functions associated with the character group of the a-adic solenoid.

Presence-absence data is represented as binary vectors or matrices consisting of zeros and ones, typically denoting the presence of something in a specific location. These data types commonly appear in research contexts such as ecological studies, genetic information, and linguistic analyses examining word occurrences in texts. Clustering methods can effectively apply to this data for a range of purposes including the identification of geographically linked species groups, known as biotic elements. Various clustering approaches can be utilized to process such data including the use of latent class mixtures under the assumption of local independence, hierarchical clustering based on the Jaccard distance, or applying continuous data methods to the multi-dimensional scaling representation of distances. These clustering methods vary conceptually and cannot easily be compared theoretically. To address this, we conduct an in-depth comparative analysis through simulation studies grounded in models for species distribution to evaluate their respective performances. 

This study has been accepted for publication in an upcoming publication titled "Innovations in multivariate statistical modelling: navigating theoretical and multidisciplinary domains," part of Springer Emerging Topics in Statistics and Biostatistics, edited by Ferreira, J., Bekker, A., Arashi, M., and Chen, D.

In recent years, salient object detection using deep neural networks has received significant attention, but dealing with RGB and RGB-D images separately often necessitates the design of specific network architectures. This paper proposes an efficient and unified structure that integrates cross-attention context extraction to effectively tackle both tasks. By effectively fusing two inputs (for RGB images) or three inputs (for RGB-D images) with a cross-attention mechanism, our framework leverages the rich information present in both RGB and depth features. This structure's simplicity and efficacy enable efficient extraction and fusion of contextual information. As shown by experimental results, our approach outperforms current state-of-the-art methods on various datasets in terms of multiple evaluation metrics.

The UM-IU@LING system for the 2019 SemEval OffensEval Task is the subject of this paper. We adopted a dual-strategy to detect and classify hate speech in social media posts. For subtask A, a BERT-based classifier was adapted and achieved a high macro F1 score of 0.8136 in evaluating test data, thereby ranking 3rd among 103 competitors. Meanwhile, in subtasks B and C, traditional Support Vector Machine and Random Forest classifiers were employed, resulting in macro F1 scores of 0.4043 and 0.4012 respectively for subtask B, and 0.4012 for subtask C.

A number, N, can be termed a palindrome if its binary format is symmetrical. In this paper, the relationship between the quotients of these symmetrical numbers is explored and several fundamental questions about the resulting sets of integers and fractions are answered. We demonstrate the feasibility of solving this problem using a precise formula, by ascertaining if an integer, N, can be expressed as a division between two identical symmetrical numbers, A and B. Upon determining representability, we pinpoint an upper limit on the value of the smallest numerical component. We then prove that a certain set of numbers has a higher frequency of occurrence within the set of all natural numbers, N. We achieve analogous results when examining quotients of numbers whose binary format is anti-palindromic, meaning the second half mirrors the reverse of the first. In this case, we investigate quotients of numbers whose binary format is anti-palindromic due to the fact that such numbers include all palindromic numbers, N.

Computed Tomography (CT) is extensively utilized in both engineering and medical fields for creating detailed images of internal structures within various subjects and objects. Since most X-ray sources emit X-rays of multiple energy levels, which vary in their absorption rates, the process of reconstructing images typically involves a reverse ray transformation process. Omitting these variations may result in image distortions such as beam hardening, which poses an additional challenge. In certain settings, the dual effects of radiation and electronic signal degradation caused by devices such as CCD cameras contribute to image degradation. A proposed variational reconstruction model effectively accounts for these two distinct types of noise as well as the polyenergetic X-ray source, and further distinguishes between materials with unique attenuation characteristics. In support of this model, the proposed iterative algorithm has been mathematically justified and verified with numerical reconstructions of data collected from a test setup.

Handwritten Text Recognition (HTR) with limited resources is a complex challenge, largely due to the scarcity of labeled data and limited language knowledge (dictionaries and language models). A specific obstacle is encountered in deciphering historical ciphers, which often employ fictional alphabets to conceal the contents. To overcome this problem, this study develops a novel data creation approach that enables one-shot learning for HTR. Our method involves generating compositional datasets for each character class in the target alphabet. These datasets are enhanced by employing an iterative image segmentation framework during training, which facilitates better segmentation precision. To validate our method, we conducted extensive experiments on two complex handwritten datasets, namely Orion-K1 and Pallas. The results demonstrate the efficacy of our proposed approach, which surpasses the performance of conventional generation techniques and dominates the state-of-the-art in low-resource HTR settings.

We have developed a novel storage approach that significantly decreases the required memory by approximately two orders of magnitude, allowing us to compute three-nucleon interaction matrix elements with more precise limits in ab initio calculations. Our scheme enables us to reach higher energies of three-nucleon interaction matrix elements than was previously achievable. We have demonstrated that our storage approach leads to converged calculations for the ground-state energy of a certain nucleus. Our study further examined how the computational methods converge when calculating three-nucleon interactions. Our findings indicate that certain computational methods converge more effectively than others at a given computational cost. We have discovered that certain computational methods that are known to be reliable in certain computational methods do not lead to converged results in our case. Our study suggests that certain aspects of these computational methods are not sufficient for calculating accurately the heavy nuclei's properties. We have also compared the computational methods' performance using the computational power of our current systems and the computational power that we can achieve with the available computational power. Our study indicates that certain computational methods are more efficient than others, including the recently developed GFB method, at a given level of computational power. We have also examined the computational methods' reliability in calculating three-nucleon interactions under certain conditions. Our study indicates that certain computational methods are more reliable than others, including the recently developed GFB method, in calculating three-nucleon interactions at a given level of computational power.

We invite undergraduate students and early graduate students to an educational introduction to one-dimensional topological phases, focusing on the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model. This will include discussions on entanglement using the correlator method and von Neumann density matrix, as well as geometric phase, polarization, and transport characteristics, all with consideration of electron-electron interactions. Hands-on numerical experiments guided by publicly available codes are used to convey the value of using topological toy models for exploring new concepts in quantum electronics.

This study examines the compactness of composition operators within Bergman spaces associated with certain bounded, convex domains in complex n-dimensional space containing non-trivial analytic circles in the boundary. Consequently, this characterizes compactness of the composition operator with a continuous symbol (limited to its closure) on the Bergman space of the polydisc.

We derived a two-loop amplitude formula for four graviton supermultiplets in AdS$_5$ times S$^5$ using a preamplitude construction, confirming the findings of Huang and Yuan. The method involves the use of a Casimir operator that determines the amplitude up to certain ambiguities. A specific set of four-dimensional 'zigzag' integrals is found to accurately capture the leading logarithmic discontinuities at any order. Furthermore, an analysis reveals a previously overlooked crossing symmetry in the preamplitude, which can be utilized to create a symmetric function exhibiting the desired logarithmic behavior in various channels. Through this approach, an explicit expression is obtained for the two-loop correction to anomalous dimensions of twist-four operators with generic spin. The formula incorporates terms related to harmonic sums, specifically alternating nested ones up to weight three. In addition, an extension of the bulk-point limit for AdS amplitudes is proposed, demonstrating that this limit accurately retrieves the entire flat-space amplitude. With the new formula, a precise calculation is possible for any of the six supergravity amplitudes, involving spins from zero to four.

High-performance computing on SIMD devices, including GPUs, has historically been challenging for object-oriented programming due to inefficiencies in memory allocation and access.  Despite this limitation, a range of applications, including real-world programs with inherent object structures, have been overlooked for parallelization opportunities.  Our research identified a particular subset of object-oriented programming called Single-Method Multiple-Objects (SMMO), which can be efficiently parallelized on SIMD devices by executing the same method across multiple objects of a given type.  To facilitate easy adoption of high-speed GPU programming for average developers, we created the DynaSOAr CUDA framework specifically tailored for SMMO applications.  This framework includes a dynamic memory allocator that is both lock-free and parallel, a data layout domain-specific language (DSL), and a do-all operation that is both parallel and efficient.  As a result, DynaSOAr offers improved memory usage, reduced fragmentation, and superior performance to leading state-of-the-art GPU memory allocators by concurrently managing both memory allocation and memory access through atomic operations.  Our experimental evaluations using various SMMO applications demonstrated that DynaSOAr yields a 2 to 7 times increase in speed over using CUDA manual memory management, with a particular improvement of up to 12 times in some cases.

We introduce family universal U(1)X models incorporating three right-handed neutrinos, by defining U(1)X as a composite of SO(10) U(1)Y and U(1)χ gauge symmetries. To incorporate quantum gravity effects, we propose the introduction of a Dirac fermion χ as a dark matter candidate that's odd under gauged Z2 symmetry post U(1)X breaking, leading to a natural realization of isospin-violating dark matter with a natural f_n/f_p ratio of -0.7, thereby evading LUX, PANDAX and XENON1T experimental constraints. Furthermore, our work encompasses the investigation of masses and mixings for Higgs and gauge bosons, LHC constraints on Z' mass, dark matter direct and indirect detection experiments, resulting in viable parameter spaces for further study. To determine LHC Z' mass bounds for generic U(1)X models, four such models have been proposed, characterized by different family universal U(1)X charges for right-handed neutrinos, leading to LHC Z' mass limits in the range of 2.8-5.2 TeV, depending on the model in question.

A specific measurement technique must be used for assessing the mechanical characteristics of straw tubes designed for charged particle detection, operating in a vacuum environment. The underlying equations that govern straw behavior when subjected to internal pressure are documented, alongside the introduction of an experimental approach in this paper to investigate strained, pressurized straw tubes. The presented research also focuses on measuring the Poisson's ratio of the straw wall for the NA62 spectrometer, with the ultimate goal of determining the minimum tension required in the straw tubes to ensure they can operate within their designated stability criteria.

In various fields, ensuring decision functions maintain their reliability in the face of unseen data is crucial. The proof system introduced here provides assurances that certain types of decision functions will retain reliability in the face of uncertain input. The framework is based on Bayesian networks, which model both dependent relationships and individual conditions. The primary contribution of this work involves adapting a previously established method for assessing function reliability to also account for potential errors. This modified approach can be represented through a more accessible version of the original problem, which comprises a network with adjusted variable limitations. The reliability guarantees can be quantified using a first-order logic formula that includes second-order components, which can be broken down into smaller sections for easier evaluation. The complexity of these segments grows logarithmically with the number of variables. The reliability guarantees can be efficiently verified within a predetermined time based on the number of variables, which allows for faster assessments when the number of variables is small.

In a supersolid Bose-Einstein condensate with a spin-orbit coupling, an accelerated impurity atom exhibits oscillations that mirror Bloch oscillations in solid matter, despite causing condensate excitements that give rise to internal phonon modes. However, these oscillations have no impact on the condensate's roton minimum position, thereby preserving its periodic matter wave pattern. Notably, the oscillations fade primarily due to wavepacket dispersal; yet, by assuming the impurity behaves as a bright soliton, the decay can be largely countered.

In a generalised quadrangle, a code is a subset of the vertices with its minimum distance determined by the shortest path between distinct elements. The elements of this subset are divided into distinct sets based on their distance from the code. Given this division, we study the transitivity of codes in quadrangles and establish both necessary and sufficient conditions for the code to be transitive. Specifically, we demonstrate that the code is transitive if and only if it forms a neighbour-transitive set in the quadrangle. Additionally, we examine partial spreads in the quadrangles and their association with transitive codes. The results obtained match the existing literature on linear codes in graphs, while further extending them to the context of quadrangles.

Located at the heart of the Milky Way lies the Central Molecular Zone (CMZ), a distinct ring-like formation, where analysis of the 870 $\mu$m continuum map from ATLASGAL, obtained via the APEX Telescope Large Area Survey of the Galaxy, revealed notable anisotropy in gas density within this area using a two-dimensional correlation function. By identifying the critical angle $\theta_{\rm half}$ and anisotropy parameter $A\equiv \frac{\pi}{4\theta_{\rm half}}-1$, it was determined that gas density in the CMZ is significantly influenced by anisotropic spatial patterns at a scale of approximately 100 parsecs. These patterns decrease in anisotropic influence as the scale diminishes to about 10 parsecs. Our research offers a quantitative assessment of the anisotropic structure of gas within the CMZ and provides a method for comparing similar regions in various areas of the galaxy.

Subjecting solid materials to an ultra-intense, femtosecond X-ray pulse from a free-electron laser causes drastic electronic excitation, triggering swift changes within the material's electronic system that unfold over the duration of the pulse. The amount of X-rays absorbed by the material becomes contingent upon the energy flux, giving rise to a unique form of X-ray absorption near edge spectroscopy. Researchers can study valence excitation on the few-femtosecond timescale with this type of XANES spectroscopy, allowing for in-depth examination of electronic dynamics close to the Fermi level.

To develop an enhanced understanding of electronic dynamics under high-fluence conditions, researchers have created a simplified theoretical model, based on recognized physical principles, to elucidate how electronic processes progress. The model examines distinct physical phenomena such as resonance absorption due to electron transitions, reduction in absorption caused by excitation-induced electron promotion, and changes in material absorption pattern resulting from broken short-range order following intense heating, all occurring over the duration of the X-ray pulse.

By incorporating time-dependent factors into each component, the model can predict how XANES spectral features evolve. Specifically, when electron transitions occur rapidly, spectral features exhibit pronounced variations. Conversely, when slower processes such as disorder-induced absorption emerge, spectral features display more gradual changes. The model also indicates that for short X-ray pulse durations, spectral features may not reach a steady state during the pulse duration, instead requiring additional time to resolve fully.
